query: What is the role of agent banks under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA)?
reference_answer: The agent banks are appointed to maintain members' CPF Investment Accounts under the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) as they have an extensive network of branches and facilities to support the investment and settlement of shares and bonds listed on the Singapore Exchange. The agent banks' electronic banking services such as ATMs are easily accessible and allow members to conveniently apply for shares or bonds during an IPO. The banks are also able to handle the complex processing of corporate actions such as bonus and rights issues, dividend payments and schemes of arrangement under the CPFIS-OA.

It takes into account not only the realised profits or losses of investments that were sold, but also the unrealised profits or losses of investments that members held during the reporting period.

Your agent bank will inform the respective product providers, except stockbrokers, of your new Investment Account number. Agent banks would not be able to inform the stockbrokers on your behalf because agent banks do not know which stockbrokers you have trading accounts with.You will need to inform all your stockbrokers about your new CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account number. If your stockbrokers use the outdated investment account number, your CPF trades will fail and you will need to settle your trades using cash.
answer: Agent banks under CPFIS-OA are appointed to manage members' CPF Investment Accounts. They offer extensive facilities for investment and share/bond settlements. They also handle corporate actions like bonus issues and dividends. Agent banks assist in applying for bonds and T-bills through their electronic portals. They inform product providers but not stockbrokers, who must be informed separately. [Document 1]
